posts.caption:
Founder log 01.

I'm Davide, and I build casdey: it wins back gym members who cancelled, in the gym's own name.

For three weeks I've emailed gym owners across Europe. 926 of them. 12 replied. 11 said no thanks. 1 said yes.

The lesson: I was asking strangers for a favour and giving nothing back. So from this week the email gives first.

I'll share the numbers here as they come in.

#gymowner #gymbusiness #buildinpublic

slides.title: How I'd write to a member [[who cancelled]].
slides.sub: Four rules, then the message itself. Save it for the next one who leaves.

slides.title: Lead with them, not a discount.
slides.body:
Open with their name and what they came to you for.
A discount in the first line reads as a sales email, not as a gym that noticed they're gone.

slides.title: No guilt.
slides.body:
Skip "we noticed you haven't been in."
People leave for real reasons: work, an injury, money, a move. Assume it was a good one.

slides.title: Give one reason to come back.
slides.body:
Something that changed since they left: a new class, a new coach, a time that suits them better.
One reason. Not five.

slides.title: Make yes easy.
slides.body:
One link that books one session.
No forms, no calls, no "let us know".

lines: Hope things are good. Since you were last in we've added [new class or time], and I thought of you.
Fancy a free session to see how it feels? Pick a time here: [booking link]

Most win-back messages fail in the first line: they open with a discount, or with guilt.

Here's how I'd write to a member who cancelled. Four rules, and the message itself at the end. Copy it, change the brackets, send it.

#gymowner #gymbusiness #memberretention

slides.title: Your ex-members have a price. [[Find yours.]]
slides.sub: All you need is your membership software and a calculator.

slides.title: Count who left.
slides.body: Members who cancelled, or just stopped coming, in the last 12 months.

slides.title: Multiply by your monthly price.
slides.body: Use your most common membership. That's what they were worth to you every month.

slides.label: a month
slides.body:
60 ex-members × €60 a month.
That money still lives in your town. It just trains somewhere else, or nowhere.

slides.title: Now the useful number.
slides.body:
You don't need all of them back. Work out what just 5 returning members are worth in a year.
5 × €60 × 12 months = €3,600.

slides.title: Send this to whoever [[runs your memberships]].
slides.body: Then work out your own number. It takes two minutes.
